is_anopheles.evidence: The study uses Anopheles gambiae strains (Kis, KdrKis, AcerKis).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper mentions the strains are homozygous for kdr L1014F and G119S ace-1 mutations (page 7, Methods section).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper states the strains are homozygous for specific mutations but does not provide genotype counts or frequencies for the populations tested; it uses established laboratory strains.

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses laboratory-reared strains (Kis, KdrKis, AcerKis) maintained in insectaries, not field-caught populations.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study testing behavioral responses of mosquito strains to various compounds.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study uses laboratory strains, not field-collected samples.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study uses laboratory strains, not field-collected samples.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study uses standard laboratory strains.

supplement.evidence: All relevant data for the laboratory strains is provided in the main text tables.

assessment.summary: This study evaluates the behavioral responses (repellency, irritancy, toxicity) of three laboratory strains of Anopheles gambiae (susceptible Kis, pyrethroid-resistant KdrKis, and OP-resistant AcerKis) to various repellents and insecticides. It is not eligible because it does not use field-collected populations.
exclusion_reasons: The study uses laboratory-reared strains, not field-collected populations.
No extractable genotype data (counts/frequencies) is provided for field populations.
